title: Choose the visual direction
question: The roll assigned the Annotated Galley. Which visual direction best supports calm reading across articles, research, and CVEs?

options.label: Annotated Galley
options.lineage: Newspaper proof sheets and reader marks
options.thesis: Read deeply without losing your bearings: annotate a document, then return to its source and shelf.
options.viewport: The reader leads: an open proof sheet with a generous text measure, discreet controls, and a genuine margin for notes and highlights. A narrow topic rail and top source line preserve bearings across articles and CVEs; return to the library for the saved register and discovery tools.
options.risk: Editorial styling can feel like a publication unless saved state, source identity, and personal annotations stay in view.

raised.raise: Repeated landmarks keep article and CVE changes comparable across updates.
Dense records use strict columns and high contrast; density never becomes texture.

options.label: Researcher’s Lab Notebook
options.lineage: Field notebooks and laboratory record books
options.thesis: One durable record for every source, with its provenance and the reader’s thinking kept together.
options.viewport: A reader’s notebook opens directly to the selected article, with provenance and dated annotations beside the text. A compact index returns to all saved sources.
options.risk: Notebook language is familiar for research tools; careful typography and a strong article register must keep the library distinctive.

options.label: Pocket Timetable Rack
options.thesis: A compact, column-led register makes a large library quick to scan.
options.viewport: A continuous article register with stable columns, a visible position rail, and each topic retaining its own heading as the reader moves.
options.case: Strong scan clarity; less recognizable as a comfortable home for long-form reading and personal notes.
options.risk: Rigid columns can squeeze titles and prose on narrow screens.

options.label: Research Wayfinding
options.thesis: Topic paths and source states stay visible at every turn.
options.viewport: A short sequence of topic and source waypoints leads from the broad library into a saved article or CVE record.
options.case: Excellent wayfinding; a route metaphor is weaker for browsing a collection and settling into a long read.
options.risk: Too much signage would turn a quiet personal tool into a loud transit hall.

options.label: Change-Aware Register
options.lineage: Boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: When a record changes, its row moves in place and stays marked until noticed.
options.viewport: Saved items form a fixed-column board; alerts remain on the changed record, while source details stay in a segmented metadata line.
options.case: Useful product clarity for updates and CVEs; less identification with a personal reading library.
options.risk: A live-board idiom can make reading feel urgent when it should feel settled.

options.label: Botanical Comparison Folio
options.thesis: Keep a stable landmark when records change over time.
options.viewport: A stable source landmark beside revision and publication dates makes update history easier to compare.
options.case: Kept: stable landmarks make time-based comparison legible across article and vulnerability records.
options.risk: A plant lifecycle is too specific to carry this mixed-source library.

options.label: High-Contrast Data Field
options.thesis: Make a dense index read as deliberate structure at a glance.
options.viewport: Use a disciplined grid for compact CVE and source metadata, with the article title and reading action remaining primary.
options.case: Kept: density belongs in column rules and tabular figures, never decorative noise.
options.risk: Pure data density weakens the calm reading task and source distinctions.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, expected library dashboard, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional sidebar and searchable article list, with saved and discovery views in familiar tabs.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, but indistinguishable from other reading dashboards by design.
